rationale: Artifact B produces a boot-config.json that is actually the required BootConfig shape; Artifact A's nested variant leaves c.productionKeyHash undefined and fails the deterministic chain check, so the core acceptance boundary (correct boot/update/policy evidence) is not met by A.

Artifact A carries genuine breadth on the operating contract (physical access, debug interfaces, peripherals, communications, update, recovery, limits, safety) but stores it in a non-conformant artifact and treats that narrative as proof — the anti-pattern the contract forbids; Artifact B keeps evidence classes, labels, and limits attached to conformant data.
